clue.text: About to be absorbed into the crowd, as they say

definitions.note: the saying 'two's company, three's a crowd'

indicators.note: something absorbed into a thing ends up inside it, so one piece goes within the letters of the other

parts.note: taken as written
RE is Latin-derived for 'concerning', a standard sense of about

explanation.surface: Something about to merge into a crowd, according to some common saying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As they say' points to the proverb 'two's company, three's a crowd', so the number is the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb equates the number with a crowd, so the idiom lets the word stand for it.

clue.text: Put down a quantity of food

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put forward a motion or paper for discussion
second meaning: the food laid out at a meal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' reads as a single verb leading into its object, but it is one meaning and the food phrase is another.
explanation.definitionFit: To table a proposal is to submit it formally; a table is also the spread of food a household provides.

clue.text: Rowdy company, somewhat plastered?

parts.note: rough behaviour is rowdy and disorderly
the cast is the company of actors in a play

explanation.surface: A noisy group of people who are a little drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' looks like slang for drunk, but the answer is a coarse plaster coating for walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughcast is a rough lime-and-gravel render, so a wall finished with it is plastered in a coarse way.

clue.text: Cumbrian river: pike's last refuge

indicators.note: the last letter of the word pike is wanted here

parts.note: the fish's name, whose last letter is taken
a den is a hiding place or retreat

explanation.surface: A fish in a northern English river finds its final hiding place.
explanation.walkthrough: Cumbria is a county in north-west England; its Eden flows to the Solway Firth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eden is a well-known river that rises in the Pennines and flows through Cumbria.

clue.text: Don't allow ghostly coverings, say, with no time for wailing spirits

parts.note: to ban is to forbid

indicators.note: having no time means that letter must come out of the coverings

parts.note: sheets are the cartoon costume of ghosts, an example signalled by 'say'

explanation.surface: A ban on sheet costumes, maybe, leaving no time for spectral wailing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish folklore a banshee is a female spirit whose keening wail foretells a death.

clue.text: I should be promoted in duty following a very advanced state of readiness

indicators.note: the duty part follows the opening letters, so it comes after them

parts.note: taken as written
A as in A-level, the Advanced level exam
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue promotion moves a letter higher, here to the front of the duty word

parts.note: a liability is an obligation or duty

explanation.surface: A soldier's case for promotion, made after a very high state of readiness.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the I out of the duty word and placing it at the front is the promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Availability is being free and ready for use when called upon.

clue.text: A line in some plan revised feature of dam?

indicators.note: a plan that is revised is redrawn, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An engineer adds a line to a draft plan for a dam.
explanation.walkthrough: A dam is also a mother animal, so the question mark nods to a fish feature, though the answer is a weir or dam structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A salmon leap is a step or ladder built into a weir or dam so fish can climb upstream.

clue.text: Annoying child denied first wrong act

indicators.note: the child is refused its opening letter

parts.note: a little terror is a badly behaved child

explanation.surface: A troublesome child is refused first go, which is a wrong thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, an act done wrongly.

clue.text: Getting old, observes small amount of money, having claimed pension at last

indicators.note: the money words take in another letter, as one claims a pension

parts.note: to see is to observe

indicators.note: only the final letter of pension is used

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken
a cent is a coin of low value

explanation.surface: Someone ageing notices a few coins after finally drawing a pension.
explanation.definitionFit: Senescent describes the process of biological ageing, growing old.

clue.text: City, European, swathed in black carpets

indicators.note: being swathed in something means being wrapped inside it

parts.note: rugs are small carpets

explanation.surface: A European city whose people are wrapped in black rugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruges is a medieval canal city in Belgium.

clue.text: Caught dancing around, around large witch's accessory?

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the second 'around' tells us the jumbled letters go round the other one
letters that dance move about, so the first 'around' is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something caught dancing round and round a large pot, like a witch.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'around's do different jobs: the first is the fodder, the second the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Witches in Macbeth and folklore stir potions in a large iron pot, so it is a stock prop.

clue.text: Possibly release diary — it covers 365 days or so

indicators.note: a possible version of the words is one of their other arrangements

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone publishing a diary that spans a year.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidereal year, measured against the fixed stars, lasts about 365 and a quarter days.

clue.text: Real German playwright, German, not British

indicators.note: not British means those letters are left out

parts.note: Bertolt Brecht, the playwright, a German

explanation.surface: A genuine German dramatist, German and not British.
explanation.definitionFit: Echt is a German loanword meaning authentic or genuine, used in English too.

clue.text: Charge lots of directors for advertising material

parts.note: a bill is a charge for goods or services
boards are groups of company directors

explanation.surface: Charging a crowd of company directors for their adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: Billboards are large outdoor hoardings that carry posters.

clue.text: Foolish insinuation, overlooking a new decline?

parts.note: dim is slang for stupid

indicators.note: overlooking something means leaving it out, so the 'a new' letter is dropped from the insinuation word

parts.note: an innuendo is a sly hint
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A daft insinuation that ignores something new in a decline.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that decline here is musical: a gradual fall in volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Diminuendo is the musical term for a steady decrease in loudness.

clue.text: Look at new type of cinema, returning in middle of week

indicators.note: the reversed letters go inside the middle of week
the two central letters of the word week

parts.note: the two central letters of this word are used

indicators.note: coming back means read in reverse

parts.note: IMAX is a giant-screen cinema format

explanation.surface: Studying a new kind of cinema that's back midweek.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine is to inspect closely.

clue.text: Isometric exercises? Sexy stuff

indicators.note: exercising the word puts its letters through their paces into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Muscle-tensing workouts as something sexy.
explanation.definitionFit: Eroticism is sexual desire or arousal, or material evoking it.

clue.text: Awkward customer to toss back endless throws

definitions.note: the word is mostly an adjective, but in Chambers also a noun for an obstructive person

indicators.note: back tells us to turn the tossing word round

parts.note: to lob is to toss high

indicators.note: the last letter of throws is dropped

parts.note: shies are throws at a target, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: A difficult customer tosses back things thrown endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshie means rebellious and uncooperative, after the Bolsheviks.

clue.text: Associated with detective, hansom lies mostly free

indicators.note: set free, the letters escape their order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something about a detective's hansom cab, which lies mostly free.
explanation.walkthrough: Sherlock Holmes famously travelled by hansom cab around Victorian London.
explanation.definitionFit: Holmesian means relating to Sherlock Holmes, the great fictional detective.

clue.text: Afropop in bar, endlessly

indicators.note: without its end, the final letter goes

parts.note: a rail is a bar

explanation.surface: African pop music playing in a bar on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: Rai is Algerian popular music blending folk and Western pop.

clue.text: Not a member of group possibly facing follow-on?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: a cricket side that is all out, which may be made to bat again

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a team bowled out well short of its opponents may be asked to follow on, batting again at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Outside means not belonging to a group; split, it gives a team dismissed in cricket.

clue.text: Meadow hired out after fine bit of advertising

indicators.note: the hired word comes after the fine one

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for meadow
to let is to rent out

explanation.surface: A field rented out after a fine, advertised by flyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a printed sheet handed out to publicise something.

clue.text: Discriminatory treatment, not primarily excellent standard

indicators.note: dropping the primary, first, letter of the excellent word

parts.note: fine means excellent
quality is a standard of excellence

explanation.surface: Treatment that is unfair, falling short of the excellent standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Inequality is unequal treatment, a lack of fairness between groups.

clue.text: Novel listing includes literary pseudonym

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer within its letters

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A book catalogue that includes a writer's pen name.
explanation.walkthrough: Emily Brontë published Wuthering Heights as Ellis Bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellis Bell was Emily Brontë's pen name, a famous literary pseudonym.

clue.text: Happen to get cheers for version under test

parts.note: to be is to exist or occur
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: A happy result earns applause for the version being tested.
explanation.definitionFit: A beta is a pre-release software version given to testers.

clue.text: Old King, trapped in a US city, in a rage

indicators.note: the king is caught inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
NY is New York
GR, Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A former monarch stuck in an American city and furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Angry means feeling or showing rage.

clue.text: A necklace item one lost among the sheets?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: one of the letters is lost from the necklace item

parts.note: a bead is strung on a necklace
A as in one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A necklace bead has gone missing in the bedclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Abed means in bed, lying between the sheets.

clue.text: One special lunar vehicle? Man provides home for one

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
a lunar lander touches down on the moon

explanation.surface: A special moon craft; a man gives it a home.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea, home to its islanders.
explanation.definitionFit: An islander lives on an island; the Isle of Man is home to such people.

clue.text: Declining upholstery material if front's absent

indicators.note: with its front missing, the first letter goes

parts.note: webbing is woven strapping used in upholstery

explanation.surface: Furniture fabric deteriorating without its front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebbing describes a tide flowing out, so something fading or diminishing.

clue.text: Malta is getting peevish with independent state

parts.note: M is Malta's international vehicle code
taken as written
sour means bad-tempered

explanation.surface: Malta gets grumpy with an independent state.
explanation.definitionFit: Missouri is a US state in the Midwest.

clue.text: Dude showing extremes of duplicity

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a man devoted to smart clothes
second meaning, read cryptically: the first and last letters of duplicity, spoken as one letter 'and' the other

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a letter puzzle rather than a dictionary sense: the ends of duplicity are D and Y, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A dude is a fashionable man, the same as a dapper fop.
